key_insight: Early pregnancy HbA1c showed only modest ability to predict gestational diabetes mellitus in this multicountry cohort, so it may help triage risk but cannot replace OGTT.
clinical_relevance: In low- and middle-income settings where OGTT is difficult to implement, early HbA1c could be a practical screening aid, but its accuracy is not strong enough for standalone diagnosis.
method: Multisite prospective cohort from PRISMA-MNH across Kenya, India, Pakistan, and Zambia
HbA1c measured before 20 weeks; OGTT after 24 weeks used to diagnose GDM by IADPSG criteria
Associations and predictive performance assessed with ROC/AUC, threshold analysis, and pooled regression estimates
evidence_signal: Among 10,918 pregnancies, HbA1c alone had an AUC of 0.65 for predicting GDM, with a 5.4% cutoff giving moderate specificity but limited sensitivity.
watch_item: Predictive performance was modest and HbA1c may be influenced by anemia, ethnicity, and other biologic factors, so implementation as a screening tool needs caution.
paper_title: Early Pregnancy Glycosylated Hemoglobin in Relation to Gestational Diabetes Mellitus and Adverse Pregnancy Outcomes: Evidence from a Multisite Low- and Middle-Income Countries Cohort
